rationale: The workflow runs CI on every push and pull request but has no concurrency cancellation, so a new push to the same branch/PR does not stop the superseded in-progress run, wasting runner time on stale checks. Adding a per-workflow/branch concurrency group with cancel-in-progress cancels superseded runs while preserving every existing step, check, and required status. This matches pattern P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE (cancel superseded runs), whose preconditions are met (same workflow/branch or PR; newer revision supersedes older checks) and whose contraindications do not apply (this is lint/build/test CI, not release or deployment work; the group keyed by github.ref keeps distinct branches isolated). Reported evidence: superseding runs can reduce duplicate work (free 1.9%, paid 4.1% VM time reduction). No permissions, secrets, publishing, or new network access is added.
